newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:
* The United States' 62-year-old welfare system is coming to an end formally on Tuesday, replaced by a decentralized system whose destiny is determined by each of the 50 states.
* U.S. President Bill Clinton is expected to endorse a tax-cut plan that would give middle-class taxpayers a bit deeper cuts than those in a bill passed last week by the Senate.
* Hong Kong moves from British colony back to its Chinese roots at the stroke of midnight on Monday.
* Regardless the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling on doctor-assisted suicide, proponents and critics of the practice agree that society must still work on providing better care for the dying.

* Dr. Betty Shabazz, the wife of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X and an inspiration herself, was remembered at a memorial service in the week after she died from burns she suffered in a fire that authorities said was set by her grandson.
* Mike Tyson may have taken at bite out of his career along with the chunk of skin he took out of rival boxer Evander Holyfield's ear as the two sparred Saturday night.
* The damage done to the Mir space station is offering a tough test to the astronauts aboard as they enter unchartered territory.
